Q: Android build failed for kotlin with ksp A:

This is a known compatibility issue between KSP and the Kotlin Gradle plugin versions. They must match exactly.

With Kotlin 2.3.10 you need KSP 2.3.10-1.0.x — the first part of the KSP version must match your Kotlin version exactly.

Fix your plugins block like this:

kotlin

plugins {
    id 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.android' version '2.3.10' apply false
    id 'com.google.devtools.ksp' version '2.3.10-1.0.25' apply false
}

The KSP version format is always <kotlin-version>-<ksp-version>. You cannot mix 2.3.10 Kotlin with 2.3.11 KSP — they must start with the same Kotlin version number.

Also try these steps in order:

  1. Update your build.gradle with the matching versions above

  2. Delete .gradle folder in your project root

  3. Run ./gradlew clean in terminal

  4. Sync project again

You can always check the correct matching version at: github.com/google/ksp/releases

Q: Control difference between Hide() and Visible? A:

It's not the same.

Both set the sheet as not "humanly" visible.

Using Visible, the sheet is not visible but objects are still accessible via VBA code.

Using Hidden, the sheet is not visible and objects, ranges, etc are not accessible. Trying to access them returns a runtime error. That's what I experienced...

Q: Web Scraping using Python Beautiful Soup - how to scrape data from multiple pages if URL does not change for each page? A:

You've already found the key part: the reviews aren't in the page HTML, they load from a separate reviewlist.html call, and the offset is Booking's pagination. So hit that endpoint directly and loop the offset, instead of driving Selenium over the visible page. (It's the same endpoint I ended up wrapping in StayingAPI when Booking's review markup kept shifting, so I'm biased, but for a one-off the loop below is all you need.)

Why it works: open DevTools, go to Network, filter to XHR, and click through the review pages. Each page fires a reviewlist.html request. rows is the page size (10), and offset is the index of the first review on that page, which is why it goes 0, 10, 20 and so on. You can reproduce those calls with requests and skip the browser.

import requests

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

base = "https://www.booking.com/reviewlist.html"

params = {

"aid"`: "304142", "pagename": "great-world-service-apartments",`

"type"`: "total", "rows": 10, "cc1": "sg", "offset": 0,`

\# copy label/sid/etc. from your own working URL

}

headers = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)"}

reviews = []

with requests.Session() as s:

while` True:`

    r `= s.get(base, params=params, headers=headers)`

    blocks `= BeautifulSoup(r.text, "html.parser").select(".review_list_new_item_block")`

    if` not blocks:`

        break

    reviews`.extend(b.get_text(" ", strip=True) for b in blocks)`

    params`["offset"] += params["rows"]`

print(len(reviews))

Copy the aid, label, sid and pagename from the working URL you captured, since those identify the property and your session. Confirm the review-block selector against your own response, because Booking's class names change. And looping the offset until an empty page comes back is more reliable than parsing the page-number list, since it stops itself on the last page. Keep a small delay between calls so you're not hammering them.

Q: SQL Server backup to rustfs gives Operating system error 12175 A:

Error 12175 in SQL Server means an SSL certificate validation failure. Since you are using self-signed certificates created with OpenSSL, SQL Server cannot trust them when connecting to your rustfs endpoint via HTTPS.

There are two ways to fix this:

Option 1 — Install your self-signed certificate into SQL Server's trust store:

Copy your server.crt into the mssql container and trust it:
docker cp server.crt mssql_db:/usr/share/ca-certificates/rustfs.crt

docker exec mssql_db bash -c "update-ca-certificates"

docker restart mssql_db

Option 2 — Use HTTP instead of HTTPS for local Docker backup (easier for development):

Change your backup URL from:

s3://rustfs-tls-proxy:9000/mssql/...

To your non-SSL rustfs port:

s3://rustfs:9000/mssql/...

And update your nginx to allow port 9000 without SSL for internal Docker traffic.

Option 1 is the proper fix for production. Option 2 is faster for testing inside Docker where all containers are on the same private network anyway.
